plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher than my value risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $20, I will bid $20 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction format where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding my true value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (my value exceeds the second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks losses if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior round history to adjust from, truthful bidding remains optimal.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, since my bid only determines whether I win, not what I pay. Bidding higher than my value risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit). Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I should bid exactly $45, my true value, to maximize expected profit.
